# Grade 7 Life Science Lesson Plan: Cellular Organelles
Date: 10/14/2026 | Teacher: Marcus Vance | Period: 3 (10:15 AM - 11:05 AM)

## Standard and Objective
- Standard: MS-LS1-2 (Develop and use a model to describe the function of a cell as a whole and ways parts of cells contribute to the function).
- Objective: SWBAT compare plant and animal cell structures by correctly identifying at least 5 shared and unique organelles on an exit ticket.

## Materials and Station Setup
| Item | Quantity | Location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compound light microscopes | 12 | Counter B |
| Prepared slides (Elodea leaf) | 14 | Tray 1 |
| Prepared slides (Cheek epithelial) | 14 | Tray 2 |
| Organelle reference cards | 28 | Student Desks |

## Instructional Sequence
- 10:15 - 10:23 AM: Warm-Up & Hook. Students complete two review questions on cell theory in science journals, then review responses.
- 10:23 - 10:35 AM: Direct Instruction. Present slides 4 through 11 covering nucleus, cell membrane, cytoplasm, mitochondria, vacuole, chloroplast, and cell wall.
- 10:35 - 10:50 AM: Partner Laboratory Investigation. Students examine both slides under 100x and 400x magnification to sketch and label structures.
- During the microscope lab, identify chloroplasts in cheek epithelial cells and record observations in lab notebooks.
- 10:50 - 11:05 AM: Formative Assessment. Administer the organelle identification exit ticket.

## Accommodations and Differentiation
- EL Support: Provide bilingual organelle reference charts with visual diagrams to Leo G. and Sofia R.
- IEP Modification: Provide reduced-choice exit ticket with a word bank for Marcus T. and Elena W.

errors.quote: identify chloroplasts in cheek epithelial cells
errors.explanation: Cheek epithelial cells are animal cells and do not contain chloroplasts; chloroplasts are found in plant cells such as the Elodea leaf specimen.
errors.fix: identify chloroplasts in Elodea leaf cells
